item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00425","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C20","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C16 directly created the liquidation framework that the child completes: it continued the Economic Stabilization Agency through October 31, 1953 under the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization specifically to wind up and liquidate its affairs. The child, effective principally November 1, then distributes the functions remaining from that liquidation among the Treasury, Office of Defense Mobilization, and Attorney General. This close temporal handoff, identical agency, shared administrator, and continuation-to-disposition sequence constitute material administrative machinery rather than merely a shared topic. C20 is a strong generic liquidation-and-transfer precedent, while C15 similarly terminates an agency and allocates its remaining functions and property, but neither is as directly connected to the child's precise liquidation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Such functions as remain in connection with the fiscal liquidation of the Economic Stabilization Agency are hereby transferred to the Secretary of the Treasury.","parent_excerpt":"The Economic Stabilization Agency ... is continued to October 31, 1953, under the direction of the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization ... for the purpose of winding up and liquidating the affairs of said Agency.","explanation":"The child takes the liquidation expressly established by C16 and assigns its remaining fiscal component after C16's October 31 endpoint."},{"child_excerpt":"The function of conducting administrative proceedings under Title IV of the Act ... is hereby transferred to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization.","parent_excerpt":"Every officer and agency of the Government having functions under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended ... shall perform the said functions subject to the direction and control of the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization.","explanation":"Both use the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization as the central recipient or controller of residual Defense Production Act functions."},{"child_excerpt":"Sections 1 and 2 of this order shall become effective November 1, 1953.","parent_excerpt":"The Economic Stabilization Agency ... is continued to October 31, 1953","explanation":"The consecutive dates reveal a designed administrative handoff from C16's temporary liquidation regime to the child's final allocation of remaining functions."}]}
